stops.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus & Properties of definite integrals
stops.inShort: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). King's property: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b − x) dx; ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx. For even/odd functions on [−a, a]: 2∫_0^a f(x) dx if even, 0 if odd.

stops.title: Reduction & Limit of a sum
stops.inShort: ∫_0^(2a) f(x) dx = 2∫_0^a f(x) dx if f(2a−x) = f(x), and 0 if f(2a−x) = −f(x).

items.f: ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx;  ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b − x) dx
items.s: Most frequently tested 4-mark proof & numerical tool.

board.text: Prove that ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx and hence evaluate ∫_0^(π/2) √(sin x) / (√(sin x) + √(cos x)) dx.
board.answer:
Proof: Put x = a − t ⇒ dx = −dt. When x = 0, t = a; when x = a, t = 0.
∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_a^0 f(a − t)(−dt) = ∫_0^a f(a − t) dt = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx.
Evaluation: Let I = ∫_0^(π/2) √(sin x)/(√(sin x) + √(cos x)) dx.
Using property: I = ∫_0^(π/2) √(cos x)/(√(cos x) + √(sin x)) dx.
Adding: 2I = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4.

points.text: Proof using substitution x = a − t
Applying property to I and adding 2I = ∫_0^(π/2) 1 dx

board.answer:
Let I = ∫_0^(π/4) log(1 + tan x) dx.
Using ∫_0^a f(x) dx = ∫_0^a f(a − x) dx:
I = ∫_0^(π/4) log(1 + tan(π/4 − x)) dx = ∫_0^(π/4) log(1 + (1 − tan x)/(1 + tan x)) dx = ∫_0^(π/4) log(2 / (1 + tan x)) dx.
I = ∫_0^(π/4) log 2 dx − I ⇒ 2I = (π/4) log 2 ⇒ I = (π/8) log 2.
